invariants.title: framework identity
invariants.summary: jQStar is an HTML-first reactive framework for server-rendered applications. It uses the real jQuery instance and does not require a virtual DOM or client-side router.

invariants.title: jquery signal boundary
invariants.summary: $ is real jQuery. A name such as $count is a reactive signal. These meanings are intentionally different.

invariants.title: csp security boundary
invariants.summary: The explicit jquery-star/csp engine performs no dynamic code construction in its entry graph. It requires trusted markup and trusted installed extensions, is not a sandbox, and does not configure or replace the page policy for scripts, styles, network endpoints, jQuery plugins, or application code.

invariants.summary: A component root uses data-jqs. Stable internal slots use data-part. Reflected state uses data-state or a documented component-specific data attribute.
invariants.content: A component root uses data-jqs. Stable internal slots use data-part. Reflected state uses data-state or a documented component-specific data attribute.

invariants.title: registry ownership
invariants.summary: The application owns component markup and block code after jqstar add copies registry recipes into it. Generic behavior stays in the jquery-star package.
invariants.content: The application owns component markup and block code after jqstar add copies registry recipes into it. Generic behavior stays in the jquery-star package.

invariants.title: patch lifecycle
invariants.summary: Server-rendered HTML remains authoritative. Use data-jqs-preserve only for a live root that must survive a patch, and use whenEnhanced() to wait for a complete patch commit.
invariants.content: Server-rendered HTML remains authoritative. Use data-jqs-preserve only for a live root that must survive a patch, and use whenEnhanced() to wait for a complete patch commit.

invariants.title: testing ownership
invariants.summary: The testing harness requires a caller-owned same-realm Window, Document, and jQuery instance. Its bounded flush covers jQStar-owned work, queued fixtures, and registered finite tasks, not arbitrary timers or real-network idleness.
invariants.content: The testing harness requires a caller-owned same-realm Window, Document, and jQuery instance. Its bounded flush covers jQStar-owned work, queued fixtures, and registered finite tasks, not arbitrary timers or real-network idleness.

invariants.title: external render ownership
invariants.summary: Turbo and htmx own requests, forms, history, focus, and DOM mutation. The shipped jquery-star/turbo and jquery-star/htmx bridges use the public render adapter only to release outgoing ownership, preserve exact approved identities, and enhance incoming roots.

guides.title: jQStar framework
guides.summary: What jQStar is, what stays on the server, and the boundaries of the current framework.
headings:
Polished UI behavior for
Datastar applications.
This website is a jQStar application.
guides.content:
v0.1.0 is now available
Polished UI behavior for
Datastar applications.
A jQuery-powered framework built for backend-first developers. Write HTML, add standard
attributes, and get accessible, interactive UIs without a build step.
Get Started →
npm install jquery-star jquery
Copy
Why jQStar
>_
No Build Step Required
Start with a script tag or the package you already use. jQStar complements your
existing server-rendered application.
⚡
Built for Datastar
Components cooperate with DOM replacements and automatically enhance HTML delivered by
Datastar.
</>
HTML is the API
Your backend renders the markup. Standard attributes declare behavior while jQStar
keeps real jQuery available.
The framework promise
A complete server-rendered development experience.
jQStar is for teams that want modern interaction without moving their entire application
into a client runtime.
Keep the server in charge
- Keep routes, validation, permissions, and data on the server.
- Keep HTML readable and useful before JavaScript runs.
- Add reactivity and rich components where they are needed.
- Update regions through HTML, JSON, or Datastar streams.
- Avoid JSX, hydration, virtual DOM ownership, and duplicated client routes.
- Continue using existing backend templates and jQuery plugins.
- Adopt it incrementally instead of rewriting the application.
What we are building for
- An excellent server-rendered development experience.
- Predictable enhancement and cleanup after HTML replacement.
- Examples for PHP, Rails, Django, Node, and similar stacks.
- Strong no-build and modular-package support.
- Accessible components that solve real application workflows.
- Optional navigation and shared state without making them mandatory.
- Migration paths from ordinary jQuery, jQuery UI, and jQuery Mobile.
$ is real jQuery. $name is a reactive signal. Named actions move
longer behavior back into JavaScript.
Built with itself
This website is a jQStar application.
The theme control, dialogs, responsive documentation, code previews, component examples,
and Component Lab all run on the same public model documented here. React is not hiding
behind the page.
Component documentation
Learn the native markup, actions, state attributes, and keyboard contract.
Read the guides →
Component Lab
Exercise the exhaustive UI, forms, data, blocks, and backend integration proof.
Open the live system →

guides.title: Introduction
guides.summary: Install jquery-star, boot an application, use real jQuery beside reactive signals, and copy registry recipes.
guides.content:
Introduction
jQStar adds reactive state, backend actions, and accessible UI behavior to ordinary
server-rendered HTML. It uses the real jQuery instance rather than replacing it with a
look-alike API.
Design philosophy: your backend generates HTML, jQStar enhances local
interaction, and Datastar can stream server changes. No virtual DOM or duplicated browser
router is required.
Install the package
jQStar 0.1 supports jQuery 4 and Node 24 or newer for package consumers and tooling.
Terminal
Copy
```
npm install jquery-star jquery
```
Import jQuery, install jQStar's root side effect, and include the optional default theme.
main.ts
Copy
```
import $ from "jquery";
import "jquery-star";
import "jquery-star/ui.css";
$("#app").star();
```
Write reactive HTML
A data-signals root owns local state. Directive expressions can read and write
signals and call the installed jQuery instance in the same expression.
counter.html
Copy
```
<section id="counter" data-signals="{ count: 0 }">
<button data-on:click="$count++; $(el).fadeOut()">
Increment and disappear
</button>
<output data-text="$count"></output>
</section>
```
$ is real jQuery. $count is a reactive signal. They are
deliberately two different things.
Boot a page-wide application
Use $.star.boot() when the document element is the application root. Use
$(selector).star() for an incrementally enhanced region.
main.ts
Copy
```
import $ from "jquery";
import "jquery-star";
$.star.boot();
```
Add source-owned components
The CLI copies editable native HTML into your application. The package supplies behavior and
the compiled theme; your project owns the resulting markup.
Terminal
Copy
```
npx jqstar init
npx jqstar list
npx jqstar add button dialog tabs toast
npx jqstar doctor
```
Continue with Datastar integration , inspect the
0.1 API , review the
finite CSP expression contract , verify an
external plugin , use the
testing harness , or open the
complete Component Lab .

guides.title: Datastar integration
guides.summary: Call backend actions and consume JSON, HTML, or Datastar SSE generated by the official SDK.
headings: Generate streams with the official SDK
guides.content:
Datastar Integration jQStar keeps localized browser behavior beside the HTML while the server can update signals and page regions through JSON, HTML, or Datastar server-sent events. One protocol boundary: jQStar consumes Datastar-compatible events. Your server must generate SSE with @starfederation/datastar-sdk , never handwritten event strings. Call the backend from HTML Built-in request actions serialize the current public signals and interpret the response by its content type. application.html Copy ```
``` GET places signals in a datastar query parameter. POST, PUT, PATCH, and DELETE use the documented JSON or form contract. Every request includes Datastar-Request: true . Response behavior Response jQStar result application/json Deep-patch signals; a null value removes a signal. text/html Morph elements by ID or the Datastar selector and mode headers. text/event-stream Apply Datastar signal and element patches as they arrive. 204 No Content Complete the request without changing the application. Generate streams with the official SDK Terminal Copy ``` npm install @starfederation/datastar-sdk ``` server.ts Copy ``` import { ServerSentEventGenerator } from "@starfederation/datastar-sdk/node"; const read = await ServerSentEventGenerator.readSignals(request); if (!read.success) { response.writeHead(400).end(read.error); return; } await ServerSentEventGenerator.stream(request, response, (stream) => { stream.patchSignals(JSON.stringify({ count: Number(read.signals.count ?? 0) + 1, })); stream.patchElements('
  • ', { selector: "#feed", mode: "append", }); }); ``` Enhancement after a patch Inserted HTML is scanned immediately. New directives, bindings, component roots, named actions, and cleanup hooks work without calling .star() again. Outer morphs preserve matching elements, focused controls, unsaved values, and existing jQuery handlers. Use data-ignore-morph for a general subtree the server must not change. Use data-jqs-preserve when a live jQStar application root must survive the patch, and await $.star.whenEnhanced() before reading newly inserted directive or component DOM. The repository's Component Lab includes real JSON, HTML, multipart, and official-SDK stream endpoints when run through the local proof server.

guides.title: Core API
guides.summary: Applications, named actions, backend actions, UI methods, scheduling, version, and lifecycle.
guides.content:
Core API
jQStar is HTML-driven, but its installed jQuery surface exposes explicit application,
action, request, lifecycle, and UI methods for code that needs programmatic control.
The root surface is the 0.1 compatibility contract. The core ,
ui , datastar , testing , and
datastar/testing package subpaths are published 0.4 previews.
Applications
API
Purpose
$(root).star()
Start an attribute-driven application on the matched root.
$(root).star(definition)
Start an application from a typed behavior definition.
$.star.boot(root?)
Boot the document element or the supplied root.
$(root).star("instance")
Read the installed application instance.
$(root).star("state")
Read its reactive state object.
$(root).star("refresh")
Refresh computed bindings and directives.
$(root).star("destroy")
Destroy that application and its owned effects.
Named actions
Use named actions for behavior that is too long for an attribute. The callback receives real
jQuery, reactive state, computed values, root and initiating elements, the event, authored
arguments, and the application instance.
main.ts Copy
```
$.star.action("removeItem", ({ $element, state }) => {
$element?.closest("li").fadeOut(180, function () {
$(this).remove();
});
state.itemCount = Math.max(0, Number(state.itemCount) - 1);
});
```
items.html Copy
```
<button data-on:click="@removeItem">Remove</button>
```
Backend actions
$.star.get , post , put , patch , and
delete return ordinary named-action functions. The same methods are available
declaratively as @get , @post , and their peers.
main.ts Copy
```
const app = $("#items").star("instance");
await app?.run($.star.post("/items", {
payload: { title: "Proof" },
pending: "saving",
error: "saveError",
retry: "never",
}));
```
UI methods
$.star.ui groups component-specific methods such as dialog.open ,
tabs.activate , menu.close , and toast.show . Named
@ui.* actions call the same behavior from HTML.
$.star.ui.enhance(root) scans newly authored component markup when an explicit
application integration needs it; normal jQStar and Datastar patches enhance automatically.
main.ts Copy
```
$.star.ui.dialog.open("#account-dialog", {
initialFocus: "#account-dialog-cancel",
});
$.star.ui.tabs.activate("#settings-tabs", "security");
$.star.ui.toast.show({
title: "Saved",
description: "Your changes are live.",
variant: "success",
});
```
Scheduling and version
$.star.nextUpdate() resolves after the next reactive update flush.
$.star.whenEnhanced() waits for pending render transactions, observer delivery,
directive and UI enhancement, and the resulting reactive work. Use it before reading DOM
inserted by an HTML or Datastar patch. $.star.version reports the installed
runtime version, and $.star.clearExpressionCache() clears the current
expression engine's cache.
Terminal disposal
$.star.dispose() permanently closes one document installation, attempts every
owned cleanup, releases its document and expression-engine claims, and returns a frozen
JSON-safe report. A cleanup failure throws StarDisposalError after the complete
sweep and retains that report. Repeated disposal returns the same report or throws the same
error object.
Continue with the CSP expression contract , the
testing harness , or the
plugin contract and conformance guide .

guides.title: CSP expressions
guides.summary: The shipped jquery-star/csp installer, finite expression grammar, capability boundary, deterministic limits, server policy, diagnostics, and compatibility migrations.
guides.content:
CSP expressions
jqstar-csp-expression/1 is the shipped finite language contract for the
jquery-star/csp expression engine. The package provides an explicit installer,
ESM and CommonJS formats, matched declarations, and a strict-policy browser proof.
CSP compatibility means no dynamic code construction in the CSP engine or
its package entry graph. It requires trusted markup and trusted installed extensions. It
is not a sandbox and does not make attacker-authored expressions safe.
The page policy—not jQStar—governs inline scripts, styles, network endpoints, third-party
jQuery plugins, and application code. Applications still own authorization, CSRF protection,
output encoding, HTML sanitization, Trusted Types, and server validation.
Two engine profiles
Profile
Language
Status
Trusted JavaScript
Current JavaScript expressions and statements, including real jQuery.
Shipped; requires unsafe-eval .
CSP
Closed finite grammar with capability-specific reads, writes, and calls.
Shipped as an explicit optional entry.
CSP selection is explicit. It does not weaken or silently replace the trusted engine, and
the compatibility root never auto-selects it.
Install the CSP runtime
Import the CSP entry directly and call installStarCSP() before installing
plugins or booting applications. Do not import the compatibility root on the same jQuery
instance because that root retains the trusted JavaScript engine.
app.ts
Copy
```
import $ from "jquery";
import { installStarCSP } from "jquery-star/csp";
import { datastarPlugin } from "jquery-star/datastar";
import { uiPlugin } from "jquery-star/ui";
const installed = installStarCSP($);
installed.star.use([datastarPlugin, uiPlugin]);
installed.star.boot(document);
```
Repeated CSP installation returns the same owner. A live incompatible engine is rejected.
Advanced hosts can pass createCSPExpressionEngine() through the explicit
jquery-star/core engine seam. Separate jQuery/kernel owners can select
different engines.
Server policy
Importing the entry does not add response headers. The installed-package proof starts from
this policy and serves scripts and styles as external same-origin assets:
Content-Security-Policy
default-src 'none'; script-src 'self'; style-src 'self'; connect-src 'self'; img-src 'self'; font-src 'self'; base-uri 'none'; object-src 'none'; frame-ancestors 'none'; form-action 'self'
Adapt allowed origins to the application. If a report names unsafe-eval , verify
that the page did not import the package root and that another script or jQuery plugin did
not construct code.
Supported expression shape
The finite profile keeps the framework meanings stable: $ is real jQuery and a
name such as $count is a reactive signal. It supports bounded literals, arrays,
plain objects, reviewed operators, conditionals, state reads and writes, event and argument
data, named actions, committed helpers, and a closed jQuery method table.
finite-profile.html
Copy
```
<section data-signals="{ count: 0, saved: false }">
<button data-on:click="$count += 1; return action('save', $count)">
Save
</button>
<output data-text="$saved ? 'Saved' : $count"></output>
</section>
```
Functions, classes, declarations, loops, exceptions, modules, arbitrary calls, ambient
globals, callbacks, and automatic semicolon insertion are not part of the language.
return and await are available only in the statement entry point.
Capability boundary
Origin
Allowed authority
$name , state , signals
Read safe paths; write only approved state paths.
computed , args , evt
Read reviewed data; event calls are limited to default and propagation control.
el , root , $el , $root
Read same-realm values and use the reviewed jQuery table within the application
root.
action('name') , @name
Invoke a source-literal registered action with bounded arguments.
Committed helper path
Invoke only that exact installed helper leaf.
The evaluator rejects constructor , prototype ,
__proto__ , call , apply , bind , reflective
lookup, accessors, inherited properties, arbitrary thenables, and any function obtained as
data. Escaped, computed, concatenated, or result-derived spellings do not bypass the check.
jQuery and trusted HTML
Selectors, HTML passed to html() , class names, attribute/property names, and
CSS property names must be source string literals. Selectors are scoped to
root and collections are bounded. Callback-taking methods, event registration,
queue control, jQuery network helpers, script evaluation, and arbitrary plugin methods are
excluded.
A CSP expression may deliberately select elements, mutate DOM and state, insert
application-trusted literal HTML, invoke an authorized action or helper, and initiate a
request through that capability. HTML responses that can add expression-bearing attributes
are therefore trusted markup. JSON signal patches, form values, events, and return data stay
data and are never reparsed as expressions.
Deterministic limits
Resource
Maximum
Source length
2,048 UTF-16 code units
Tokens / AST nodes / evaluation steps
512 / 256 / 128
Nesting / path segments / call arguments
16 / 8 / 8
Literal entries / collection size
64 / 128
Approved asynchronous chain
8
Errors carry a stable CSP_* code, compile or evaluate phase, grammar version,
authored attribute and source, zero-based UTF-16 offsets, and 1-based line and column spans.
Diagnostics do not serialize state, DOM, credentials, response values, arguments, or
rejection causes.
Migration from trusted JavaScript
Most current public expressions are exact finite-profile matches. Ambient JavaScript and
arbitrary jQuery extensions move behind registered, application-owned actions or helpers.
Trusted expression
CSP migration
console.log($count)
Register and call an application diagnostic action or helper.
$(el).datepicker()
Register an integration action that owns the plugin call.
Promise.resolve($count)
Return an approved asynchronous result from an action or helper and await it.
this
Use the explicit el binding.
Version and verification
The versioned contract combines the grammar, capabilities, limits, diagnostics, accepted and
denied source, adversarial payloads, executable-context recipes, shared-engine mapping, and
public-example inventory. Raising a limit or changing accepted source requires a new grammar
version and review. The repository command npm run test:csp-contract validates
the frozen inputs and prints their combined SHA-256 digest.
Package quality runs the exact ESM and CommonJS artifacts plus this public interaction shape
in Chromium, Firefox, and WebKit. Continue with the
Core API ,
plugin boundary , or
testing harness .

guides.title: Turbo and htmx interoperability
guides.summary: Install the shipped Turbo and htmx lifecycle bridges and review their tested version boundaries, preservation, focus ownership, and limits.
guides.content:
Turbo and htmx interoperability
jQStar has tested bridges for wrapping external DOM renders without taking over the host
library. The jquery-star/turbo and jquery-star/htmx previews both
ship now.
One ownership seam: the host sends requests and mutates the DOM. A bridge
uses createRenderAdapter() only to release outgoing jQStar roots, preserve
exact approved identities, enhance incoming roots, and await the barrier.
Tested version boundaries
Host
Approved evidence range
Tested packages
Turbo
>=8.0.21 <8.1.0
8.0.21 and 8.0.23
htmx
>=2.0.0 <2.1.0
2.0.0 and 2.0.10
Missing, prerelease, unknown, and out-of-range versions fail before a bridge installs
listeners. The htmx bridge also requires the explicit version to match
htmx.version . jQStar does not auto-detect or load either host.
Install the Turbo bridge
Explicit Turbo capability and version
```
import * as Turbo from "@hotwired/turbo";
import $ from "jquery";
import { installStarCore } from "jquery-star/core";
import { createTurboBridge } from "jquery-star/turbo";
const { star } = installStarCore($);
const bridge = star.use(
createTurboBridge({ $, Turbo, version: "8.0.23" }),
);
await bridge.whenIdle();
```
Use the exact installed Turbo package version. Importing the bridge is inert. Installing it
registers document-scoped public event listeners but never calls Turbo start or navigation
APIs. bridge.dispose() removes those listeners without disposing Turbo or the
jQStar kernel.
Install the htmx bridge
Explicit htmx capability and version
```
import htmx from "htmx.org";
import $ from "jquery";
import { installStarCore } from "jquery-star/core";
import { createHtmxBridge } from "jquery-star/htmx";
const { star } = installStarCore($);
const bridge = star.use(
createHtmxBridge({ $, htmx, version: "2.0.10" }),
);
await bridge.whenIdle();
```
Use the exact installed htmx package version. Importing the jQStar bridge is inert.
Installing it registers document-scoped public lifecycle listeners but never calls
htmx.ajax() , htmx.process() , htmx.swap() , or
htmx.trigger() . whenIdle() waits for bridge-owned render and
jQStar enhancement work, not arbitrary htmx requests or network idleness.
Lifecycle
External render state machine
```
prepared
-> removing
-> externally-mutated
-> enhancing
-> committed
Terminal alternatives: canceled or failed
```
Cancellable intent creates no render transaction. A real mutation starts at Turbo's pausable
document or Frame render callback, or at the approved htmx swap and cleanup seam. Every
opened transaction commits or fails once.
Host-specific differences
Flow
Observed contract
Turbo document or Frame
Wrap detail.render , then commit before host completion.
Turbo form
submit-end and before-visit can reverse across browsers.
Both precede render.
htmx replacement
Deduplicate nested cleanup, commit after the host swap, and finish at settle.
htmx delete
Cleanup and afterRequest occur without afterSwap or
afterSettle .
htmx no-swap
afterSwap may fire even when no target mutation occurs.
Preservation and focus
data-jqs-preserve remains the core marker. The Turbo bridge also passes an
exact old data-turbo-permanent element, and the htmx bridge does the same for
hx-preserve . In each case, the old element must be connected, inside the
outgoing boundary, uniquely identified, matched once in the incoming content, and retained
after mutation. Duplicate, missing, disconnected, moved, or cross-document candidates are
cleaned and diagnosed.
The tested hosts retain DOM and control-value identity for valid permanent elements but can
move focus to the activated control. Focus remains host-owned. A bridge must not add a focus
correction unless a later contract explicitly approves and tests one.
Proof and limits
Actual boundary packages run in Chromium, Firefox, and WebKit against native links and
forms, document and region changes, history, cache, preservation, cancellation, no-content
responses, and failures. Semantic traces omit URLs, form values, headers, bodies, HTML, DOM
objects, signal values, and raw errors.
Turbo Streams, morph refresh, custom Turbo renderers, custom htmx swap extensions, shadow or
cross-document targets, and script execution guarantees are outside this contract. Read the
complete
repository contract
for every stable mapping ID and update rule.
htmx troubleshooting
-
An installation error usually means the explicit version differs from
htmx.version , falls outside >=2.0.0 <2.1.0 , or the
capability is incomplete.
-
A prevented swap can indicate a disconnected target, unsupported swap style, duplicate
main swap, or overlapping active boundary. Pass onError and inspect
bridge.observations() for redacted evidence.
-
A recreated preserved root needs the same unique, non-empty id on the old and
incoming hx-preserve or data-jqs-preserve element.
-
A pending whenIdle() is waiting for a mapped htmx terminal event or jQStar
enhancement. Call dispose() during shutdown.

guides.title: Components
guides.summary: Native component semantics, data-jqs roots, data-part slots, state attributes, and source-owned recipes.
guides.content:
Components
jQStar ships 102 source-owned component recipes and seven composed application blocks.
Native semantics do the platform work; data-jqs roots and
data-part slots add consistent behavior, state, and styling hooks.
Dialog
Native modality, focus containment and return, lifecycle events, and sheets.
Read Dialog →
Dropdown
Roving focus, typeahead, checkbox/radio items, positioning, and dismissal.
Read Dropdown →
Tabs
Automatic or manual activation, stable values, orientation, and keyboard movement.
Read Tabs →
Toast
Accessible announcements, pausable timers, actions, keyboard focus, and swipe.
Read Toast →
The component contract
-
Native elements first: buttons, forms, details, dialog, tables, links,
progress, and other platform semantics remain real.
-
Stable anatomy: data-part identifies structural slots
without coupling behavior to decorative classes.
-
Visible state: documented attributes such as data-state ,
data-value , and ARIA state remain inspectable.
-
Keyboard and focus: composite widgets implement their documented WAI-ARIA
interaction model and focus ownership.
-
Server replacement: newly patched roots enhance automatically and removed
roots release owned behavior.
-
Source ownership: the CLI copies ordinary HTML that applications can
edit; jQStar supplies the reusable runtime.
Install recipes
Terminal Copy
```
npx jqstar list --type component
npx jqstar add dialog dropdown-menu tabs toast
npx jqstar list --type block
```
Explore the complete system
The first hand-authored guides establish the documentation pattern. The
Component Lab remains the exhaustive live proof for
all recipes, composed blocks, forms, data tables, backend requests, and Datastar streams.

Review changes before saving.

 ``` API Reference Attribute Element Description Dialog The native modal owner and component root. data-part="content" Container The styled surface inside the browser top layer. title / description Heading and text Parts used to establish accessible dialog relationships. data-part="footer" Container Optional action layout. data-close-on-backdrop Dialog Opts into dismissal when the native backdrop is pressed. data-variant="sheet" Dialog Uses the same dialog behavior in a side-docked composition. Keyboard Interactions - Enter / Space Activates the ordinary trigger button. - Tab / Shift+Tab Moves through focusable controls while native modality contains focus. - Escape Closes the dialog unless the cancel event is prevented, then restores trigger focus. Opening emits cancelable jquery-star:dialog:before-open and final open events; closing follows the same before/final pattern. JavaScript can call $.star.ui.dialog.open() and close() directly.

guides.title: Dropdown
guides.summary: Menu-button markup with roving focus, typeahead, selection, and collision-aware positioning.
guides.content:
Dropdown A popup action menu with managed positioning, roving focus, typeahead, selection, disabled items, checkbox and radio state, dismissal, and trigger focus return. Preview Code Project actions Edit project Show preview Archive Delete permanently dropdown-menu.html Copy ```
``` API Reference Contract Purpose data-jqs="menu" The positioned menu root. data-part="trigger" The button that opens and receives focus after dismissal. data-part="content" The generated menu surface and accessible menu owner. item / checkbox-item / radio-item Selectable item types with stable data-value identities. data-disabled Keeps an item focusable for discovery but prevents selection. data-side / data-align Preferred floating placement; collision handling remains automatic. Keyboard Interactions - Enter / Space Opens the menu or selects the focused item. - Arrow Up / Down Moves focus among items and wraps at either end. - Home / End Moves to the first or last menu item. - Typeahead Moves to an item whose label starts with the typed characters. - Escape Closes the menu and restores focus to its trigger. The cancelable jquery-star:menu:select event can prevent a selection. Add data-close-on-select="false" when a menu should remain open. Programmatic and named actions are available under $.star.ui.menu and @ui.menu.* .

guides.title: Tabs
guides.summary: Keyboard-accessible tabs with stable values and automatic or manual activation.
guides.content:
Tabs A set of named panels with generated tab semantics, roving focus, automatic or manual activation, horizontal or vertical orientation, and cancelable value changes. Preview Code Account Security Notifications Account Update the public name and email attached to this workspace. Security Review active sessions and rotate project credentials. Notifications Choose which server events should send an alert. tabs.html Copy ```
Account settings
Security settings
``` API Reference Contract Purpose data-jqs="tabs" The component root; data-value stores the active stable value. data-part="list" The labeled tab list and orientation owner. data-part="trigger" A tab whose value matches one panel. data-part="panel" The associated tab panel. data-activation="manual" Moves focus without changing panels until Enter or Space. data-orientation="vertical" Uses Up and Down instead of Left and Right movement. Keyboard Interactions - Left / Right Moves through horizontal tabs and activates on focus by default. - Up / Down Moves through a vertical tab list. - Home / End Moves to the first or last enabled tab. - Enter / Space Activates the focused tab when manual activation is configured. Changes emit cancelable jquery-star:tabs:before-change and final jquery-star:tabs:change events. Call $.star.ui.tabs.activate('#settings-tabs', 'security') or the equivalent @ui.tabs.activate action for programmatic selection.

guides.title: Toast
guides.summary: Accessible non-modal notifications with timers, actions, focus, and swipe dismissal.
guides.content:
Toast A temporary, non-modal notification with accessible announcements, optional actions, pausable duration, keyboard access, and pointer swipe dismissal. Preview Code Show notification toast.html Copy ```
``` API Reference Option Purpose title Required concise notification heading. description Optional supporting detail. variant default , success , warning , or danger . duration Dismissal delay in milliseconds. Passive toasts default to five seconds. action An optional authored action; action toasts remain until dismissed unless duration is explicit. data-jqs="toast-viewport" The page-level notification and keyboard-focus owner. Keyboard Interactions - F8 Moves focus to the notification viewport. - Tab Moves among toast actions and close controls. - Escape Dismisses the currently focused toast. - Hover / Focus Pauses the active timer; it also pauses on window blur and hidden tabs. $.star.ui.toast.show() returns the created toast. Use dismiss() or clear() to remove notifications programmatically. The equivalent named actions are @ui.toast.show , @ui.toast.dismiss , and @ui.toast.clear .
